decisions.summary: T147's left rule widened from plan reviews to every non-plan-review pass, read by a new left/whose.rs, through the one owed set the first pass, the push's row and make land-tooling all read
decisions.why: The task line names a landing refused on other started tasks' record and pop-up check passes. Widening to every non-plan-review pass does not drop a row: each left pass is still owed by its own task's landing or session, and the refusal stays on everything not attributable to another started, unticked task. No GM clause or FR touches the ledger refusal, so this narrows nothing asked.

decisions.summary: Whose a pass is: first source naming a task, in own.rs's order - own words (logged subject, check-bundle -t<n> suffix, meta description), then builder (parentAgentId's brief), then page session (index.txt brief's feature and first-line task, else file name); prompt bodies never read
decisions.why: A design of the attribution the task needs, grounded in a dated measurement (25 of 26 named by page session, 1 by builder) and in the measured fact that prompt bodies name unrelated tasks. Implements the task; narrows nothing.

decisions.summary: A bare task id takes the feature that started it (event_log_hooks::started); a number names its unique specs/<n>-*
decisions.why: Resolution detail needed to attribute a pass; carries no carve-out from the task line.

decisions.summary: A pass is left only where its task is STARTED (task-starts.jsonl), not merely open
decisions.why: The task line itself says 'other started tasks''. An open task nobody started has no landing or session coming to write the row, so leaving its pass would lose the row.

decisions.summary: A pass of a ticked task (in tasks.md or tasks-done.md) still refuses, though task-starts.jsonl records it as started
decisions.why: The task line's 'started tasks' are tasks whose own landings and sessions will write their rows; a ticked task's landing has already happened, so leaving its pass would leave the row unwritten forever, defeating the ledger. task-starts.jsonl keeps every landed task's start (740 rows), so 'started' alone would leave almost everything. No known instance is left: the after-measurement refuses 3 passes, all the landing's own. A hypothetical refusal is not a known defect left.

decisions.summary: A pass naming a task never started still refuses
decisions.why: Outside the task line (not a started task), no landing or session is coming to write it, and the after-measurement shows no such pass in today's owed set: no known defect left.

decisions.summary: A pass whose every source names no task still refuses every landing until its session writes its row (found and left, judged working as designed, not filed)
decisions.why: Not a pass of another started task, so outside the task line; no landing can know whose it is, and leaving it would let an unattributable pass escape the ledger. None of the 26 measured owed passes named nothing (all were attributed), and the after-measurement's 3 refusals are the landing's own, so no known instance is left unfixed.

decisions.summary: The landing's own passes, by any source, bare or with its feature, still refuse with make ledger-owed WRITE= named
decisions.why: The task line is about OTHER tasks' passes; the landing's own are writable by WRITE= as the landing session's, so refusing them is the existing behavior the task leaves intact.

decisions.summary: Plan-review passes keep T147's rule unchanged
decisions.why: The task line names record and pop-up check passes; plan reviews are T147's already-settled case.

decisions.summary: 449 T258's own.rs is not reused as code (it lives in l7r_guard, which no gate crate may name per check guard-deps); whose.rs reads the same sources after the fact from l7r_shared, regexes copied; no guard source edited
decisions.why: Implementation choice forced by the T66 crate rule; same sources and order, no change to what the task delivers.

decisions.summary: Transcripts listed once per refusal (settle::Transcripts made pub(super) and shared), only for passes whose subject names no task
decisions.why: Cost choice inside the task; attribution unchanged.

decisions.summary: note() reworded to 'the passes of N open task(s) left to their own landings and sessions (451 T147, T157), which write their rows'; T147's pins follow
decisions.why: Message follows the widened rule; narrows nothing.

decisions.summary: The heading's note that LEDGER_ROWS_OK does not reach the first pass is not addressed; the escape's reach stays as it is (unlabeled by the author)
decisions.why: The task line's subject is the landing refused on other tasks' passes; the escape's reach is given as why that refusal had no way out. Once the first pass refuses only passes the running session can write (WRITE=), the way out exists, and the after-measurement shows the observed refusal cleared. No request clause or FR asks for the escape to reach the first pass, and no remaining refusal without a remedy is known.

decisions.summary: Two pins (left/tests.rs reading test, land inproc.rs first-pass test), each shown red with clues.left_to stubbed
decisions.why: Enforcement of the task's own behavior (FR-012's red-first practice); serves the task, not unrequested scope.

decisions.summary: Every rule lives in the existing scratch-sweep guard, so the cache has one cleaner.
decisions.why: Where the cleanup lives is how it is built, not how much of it there is. It serves 'clean up after ourselves in terms of the file system' and drops nothing.

decisions.summary: make done, make land and make closing-checks refuse below L7R_DISK_FLOOR_GB (15, GUESS) free. The refusal names the largest build directories, what cache-clean would free, the scratch worktrees and the DISK_OK escape, which is recorded.
decisions.why: This is the 'without us realizing it' half of the GM's words, enforced: a gate stops before the disk fills. The recorded escape is the project's standing guard rule. 15 is a knob marked GUESS, and the 4.56/24.77/31 GB figures that back it each carry a date and a method.

decisions.summary: make cache-clean [DRY=1] [HOURS=n] takes the cache's share of the sweep once idle past 12 h (GUESS). It is refused while any cargo/rustc/clippy/llvm-cov process runs, and a build directory a live process or a live run member holds is kept whole.
decisions.why: This is the cleanup the GM asked for. Not deleting under a running build is a physical constraint: deleting there would corrupt it and force the cold rebuild the GM's 'reusing the same build cache' point warns against. The floor still catches a machine that is never idle. The machine-wide refusal is broader than the per-target in_use check strictly needs, but that is a design choice and not a fidelity matter.

decisions.summary: A build directory is live when its name belongs to a clone, the mirror, a clone's -land/-tooling/-land-tooling, or a registered worktree whose tree exists. Because four worktrees share 'wt', its cache stays while any of them exists.
decisions.why: This fixes a measured defect, the old rule judging 'wt' dead, and keeps the cache that live work reuses, which is the GM's stated intention.

decisions.summary: A build directory goes whole only when no code path builds into its name AND every tree its dep-info names is gone. One with no dep-info cannot be proven dead and is kept. rc, clone and tree are kept; head is taken.
decisions.why: It narrows the cleanup: some directories that may be dead are kept. The GM's own words imply the exception: 'your points about reusing the same build cache and whatnot are well taken... you have correctly understood my intention'. The measured case shows what the literal reading would do. Presumed-dead deletion would have taken rc (11 GB, a live scratch clone's checks target) plus clone and tree, which current code builds into, and that is the cold-rebuild cost the GM accepted as a reason. The purpose ('not have 30 gigs... eaten without us realizing it') is still met for what is kept, because the floor refuses and names the largest build directories, live or dead. The exception covers three cases, ruled separately: (a) a name a code path builds into is reused by construction, so legitimate; (b) a tree its dep-info names still exists is live by evidence, so legitimate; (c) no dep-info, so nothing to prove from, kept and surfaced by the floor's listing, legitimate on the same 'no loss of the cache' ground and bounded by the floor.

decisions.summary: Keep each crate's newest SIXTEEN variants, not four, restating the task line's 'the newest per crate' as a count. KEPT 4 -> 16.
decisions.why: It keeps more than the task line's literal 'newest' would. Applied literally, that rule defeats the purpose the GM endorsed, reusing the build cache. It was measured: one landing gate touched 13 live l7r_mode_a variants, so keeping one or four takes variants a live build is using and forces rebuilds. The size budget still takes every variant past sixteen when the cache is over 100 GB, and the floor still refuses, so the GM's 'without us realizing it' purpose is not gutted. The task line is the session's wording, not the GM's; the GM's words do not fix a count.

decisions.summary: Past L7R_CACHE_BUDGET_GB (100, GUESS), the cleanup and the day's sweep take every dead tree's directory and every variant past sixteen, whatever its age. They never take one in use and never run while a build runs.
decisions.why: This adds cleanup in service of the request. The 100 GB knob is marked GUESS and is backed by dated du figures.

decisions.summary: The day's sweep removes this uid's /tmp/t<N>... and /tmp/tmp.* idle past 24 h (GUESS), and session task outputs idle past 24 h, a live session's included. A held-open output, and an entry holding a registered worktree, stay.
decisions.why: This is file-system cleanup the GM asked for. Keeping files that are held open or that hold a worktree prevents breaking live work; it is not a carve-out from 'clean up'. The 24 h split carries the host's dated measurement.

decisions.summary: A session's first prompt starts the sweep. The plan hooks it on the same UserPromptSubmit event that clone-sync uses, but from the sweep's own guard rather than from a call inside clone_sync_hooks. The plan labels this a deviation from the task line's '(the clone-sync prompt hook)'.
decisions.why: Ruled as the plan asks. It narrows nothing: the trigger is the same (a session's first prompt), the effect is the same (the sweep starts however recent the day's sweep was), and only the file the call sits in differs. No case the task line covers goes unswept, so it is not an exception and needs no ruling. Keeping the period, lock and detached start in one place is a placement choice. The GM asked for the cleanup, not for its host module.

decisions.summary: After a successful make land, the landed tasks' /tmp/t<N>* are removed. When another feature started a task of the same number within the day, removal is left to the 24 h age rule, and the plan says so.
decisions.why: The cleanup still happens, by the age rule within a day, so nothing is left uncleaned. Removing at once would delete another feature's live scratch (measured: 449 T158 and 451 T158 share /tmp/t158), which is destroying work, not cleaning up after ourselves.

decisions.summary: A scratch worktree is removed only when it is idle 24 h, not held, its HEAD is on a ref, and git worktree remove takes it without --force. Every other worktree is named with its idle hours, its build directory and the --force command, not removed. The plan labels this decision.
decisions.why: It narrows the cleanup: dirty or ref-less idle worktrees, and their build directories, which stay live through the registered-name rule, are named rather than removed. Removing a worktree with uncommitted files or a commit no ref holds destroys work that cannot be recovered. 'Clean up after ourselves' does not reach that, and the plan records that it cannot tell which task made a worktree, so it cannot tell whether anyone still wants it. The earlier review's concern, 'naming is an instruction, not the cleanup', is answered two ways. Every worktree that can be removed without loss now is removed. And the rest is not left to an instruction: the floor refuses done/land/closing-checks and names them, so 'without us realizing it' holds as real enforcement.

decisions.summary: The scratch-sweep guard's unit tests now use fixture paths for the cache, clones, mirror and /tmp, not the machine's real ones. This fixes the real worktree /tmp/t216/wt that a test removed.
decisions.why: This fixes a defect found in the task, an instance of the cleanup reaching real data. It is fixed here and not deferred.

decisions.summary: The clone's guard build link failure was fixed by hand (tool-profile artifacts and incremental sessions removed, rebuilt). No rule is added because its cause is not proven.
decisions.why: The defect, a build that fails, is fixed in this task. Adding no rule for an unproven cause is not a defect left unfixed.

decisions.summary: The task is classed 'Performance work? no' (disk hygiene); the gate's cost is one df.
decisions.why: The GM's words on T158 ask for cleanup and do not call it performance or measurement work. Classing it this way narrows nothing T158 was asked to do.

decisions.summary: rust/mode_a's armory pool test takes each pool sheet from crate::sweep::sheet (hand sheet as tracked, generated exception composed from its tracked compound.json), asserting which two were composed
decisions.why: Fixes the defect the task line names (a gate red in every tree that has not drawn two sheets: a check refusing good work) by the mechanism 449 T211/T252 already require; nothing drawn changes.

decisions.id: D2 the end-to-end test pages the sweep's text
decisions.summary: pool_sweep's end-to-end test hands page::held::outcomes each pool sheet's path with its swept text and asserts six sheets, two composed; outcomes (cfg(test)) takes (path, text) and reads no sheet
decisions.why: Found by the task's own 'which tests read an ignored file' census: a test whose subject changed with the tree's disk is a check that answers differently on the same code, a defect of the same class, fixed in the task rather than left; test-only signature change.

decisions.summary: a_generated_sheet_with_its_armory_off_its_roll_is_refused: the county example's spec moved, composed in a scratch dir, the check's one finding naming the roll
decisions.why: Pins that the fixed test still catches what it exists to catch (constitution: a ported or changed check is shown to work by its red case); enforcement of the requested fix, not new behavior.

decisions.id: D4 generate, not fixture or skip
decisions.summary: the generated sheets are composed in the test rather than kept as fixtures or skipped
decisions.why: A fixture cannot see a spec change (shown by the moved-spec run: the old disk-reading test could not), and a skip drops the two sheets from the check; generating is the only route that keeps the test's purpose.

decisions.id: D5 tests over 449 FR-008's tenth of a second
decisions.summary: the pool test (two composes, 0.15-0.20 s user) lands over FR-008's bar and the red-case test (one compose, 0.06-0.10 s user) at it; make test-times reports, never refuses
decisions.why: The block's own two reasons (the standing composing tests are over too; test-times never refuses) are precedent and weak enforcement and carry no weight. What carries it: the compose is the thing the test exists to exercise, and one compose alone measures 0.06-0.10 s, so no test that judges a generated sheet as the sweep composes it is reliably under the bar; the only sub-bar routes are the disk read 449 T211/T252 forbid or a fixture the moved-spec run shows is blind, so the literal rule would defeat the test's purpose. Ruled per test: the pool test is over on two composes, the red-case test at the bar on one; the end-to-end test is FR-008's own end-to-end exception. The overrun is not a wrong outcome (constitution XIV's defect definition), and the plan states it openly with its measurements.

decisions.id: D6 the three rust/gate/crates/pool tests unchanged
decisions.summary: the real-pool tests that list a folder's ignored files by name are left as they are
decisions.why: They assert folders, rows and names, a map's kind read from tracked files, and are green in a tree with no ignored file (54 passed in the clean clone); a difference that is not a defect, which fix-all-known-bugs does not reach.

decisions.summary: which crates read generated output rests on the Cargo.toml reads, the CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR/top()/toplevel() and relative-path/current_dir greps, and a clean-clone run of the three reading crates and rust/gate
decisions.why: The search space is named per step with its method; the one thing not run (other crates) is stated as resting on the reading, and those crates' declared reads hold only caches, a fixture lockfile whose reader copies tracked files, and rust/gate's development-secrets.ini (rust/gate green in the clean clone).

decisions.id: D8 found and left none; performance work no
decisions.summary: nothing deferred; the task is not classed as performance work
decisions.why: Nothing the block reports is a defect left: the standing over-bar composing test is a timing difference, not a wrong outcome, and the gate/pool tests pass in a clean tree; the task makes a verdict tree-independent and speeds nothing, so 'no' is the plain reading.

decisions.why: Fixes the observed defect the task line names (a gate red in every tree that had not drawn two sheets: rust/mode_a 1 failed NotFound in a fresh tree, observed 2026-11-22 and 2026-11-26) by the rule the crate already follows (449 T211/T252: a generated exception is composed, never read from its svg). Fixing a known defect in the step it is found in is what the GM asked (fix all known bugs as we go). No map, check or roll changes.

decisions.summary: Which tests read an ignored file is found by a stated search: git ls-files -o -i of the ignored files, grep over rust/**/*.rs for CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR/top()/toplevel() with each hit read, each Cargo.toml's declared reads, and every declaring crate's tests run in a scratch clone holding no ignored file.
decisions.why: The enumeration carries its search space and is derived from the mechanism (what a test reads, and what fails when the files are absent - the scratch-clone run), not from a name. Nothing is narrowed by it.

decisions.summary: The end-to-end test the_pages_and_the_country_shrine_are_drawn_end_to_end, green in either tree but paging four or six sheets from whatever stood on disk, is also changed to page all six from the sweep's text and assert six sheets, two composed.
decisions.why: Same defect class as the task line's (a test whose subject depends on ignored files on disk), found by the census the task asked for; making a check's subject independent of the tree is the fix itself, not unrequested scope. Test-only.

decisions.summary: page/held.rs (a cfg(test) module): outcomes takes (path, text) and reads no sheet; the path still names the page and finds its notes.
decisions.why: The mechanism the end-to-end fix needs; test-only, no drawn or shipped behavior changes.

decisions.summary: Generate (compose in process) rather than check in a fixture or skip; the composing tests measured 0.21-0.22 s (least of five, load average near 250), over 449 FR-008's tenth-of-a-second bar as measured there, reported by make test-times and not otherwise addressed.
decisions.why: Not a narrowing of 451's request or spec, neither of which carries 449 FR-008; weighed against it anyway: a fixture cannot see a spec change (the plan's red-on-a-real-defect run shows the old disk-reading test could not), a skip drops the check, and reading the disk is the defect, so composing is the only form that keeps the check doing its job and obeys 449 T211/T252; the crate's standing composing tests stand at 0.27 s and 0.40 s under the same load, and the timings were taken at load ~250 with no quiet-machine figure, so the over-the-bar state is not established. A test some tenths of a second slower is not a wrong outcome (constitution XIV's defect definition), so nothing known is left.

decisions.summary: A new test a_generated_sheet_with_its_armory_off_its_roll_is_refused keeps the measured break (armory moved to x 92.5 in a scratch compose, refused naming the roll); the pool test shown red on the moved spec and green restored.
decisions.why: Enforcement of the fix: its only effect is to prove the armory check still fails on an armory off its roll once it reads composed sheets. Serves the request; not unrequested scope.

decisions.summary: The three real-pool tests of rust/gate/crates/pool list ignored files by name and are left unchanged.
decisions.why: They are green in either tree, assert folders, rows and names with a map's kind read from tracked files, and passed in the scratch clone with no ignored file (54 passed, measured 2026-11-26): a difference from the others' form, not a wrong outcome, so not a defect and nothing known is carried forward.

decisions.summary: Exit green: the first tier green on a clone with no generated sheet (362 passed, lint and format clean, no ignored file before or after) and in this tree; red: recorded and set down, an impossibility claim ruled through make arbiter-ask; one landing, no dependency.
decisions.why: The done condition measures the task line's goal directly (a tree that has drawn nothing passes rust/mode_a's tests) and narrows nothing.

blocks: ### T159 (2026-11-22: 451 T154's trial ran the coverage gate in a new worktree and `rust/mode_a` came back 334 passed, 1 failed, NotFound; 2026-11-26: seven pool builders reported the same red "apart" on their full static runs, and two drew the sheets by hand to get past it)

decisions.id: D1 compose, never read the ignored svg
decisions.summary: rust/mode_a's armory pool test takes each pool sheet from crate::sweep::sheet (hand sheet as tracked, generated exception composed from its tracked compound.json), asserting which two were composed
decisions.why: Fixes the defect the task line names (a gate red in every tree that has not drawn two sheets: a check refusing good work) by the mechanism 449 T211/T252 already require; nothing drawn changes.

decisions.id: D2 the end-to-end test pages the sweep's text
decisions.summary: pool_sweep's end-to-end test hands page::held::outcomes each pool sheet's path with its swept text and asserts six sheets, two composed; outcomes (cfg(test)) takes (path, text) and reads no sheet
decisions.why: Found by the task's own 'which tests read an ignored file' census: a test whose subject changed with the tree's disk is a check that answers differently on the same code, a defect of the same class, fixed in the task rather than left; test-only signature change.

decisions.summary: a_generated_sheet_with_its_armory_off_its_roll_is_refused: the county example's spec moved, composed in a scratch dir, the check's one finding naming the roll
decisions.why: Pins that the fixed test still catches what it exists to catch (constitution: a ported or changed check is shown to work by its red case); enforcement of the requested fix, not new behavior.

decisions.id: D4 generate, not fixture or skip
decisions.summary: the generated sheets are composed in the test rather than kept as fixtures or skipped
decisions.why: A fixture cannot see a spec change (shown by the moved-spec run: the old disk-reading test could not), and a skip drops the two sheets from the check; generating is the only route that keeps the test's purpose.

decisions.id: D5 tests over 449 FR-008's tenth of a second
decisions.summary: the pool test (two composes, 0.15-0.20 s user) lands over FR-008's bar and the red-case test (one compose, 0.06-0.10 s user) at it; make test-times reports, never refuses
decisions.why: The block's own two reasons (the standing composing tests are over too; test-times never refuses) are precedent and weak enforcement and carry no weight. What carries it: the compose is the thing the test exists to exercise, and one compose alone measures 0.06-0.10 s, so no test that judges a generated sheet as the sweep composes it is reliably under the bar; the only sub-bar routes are the disk read 449 T211/T252 forbid or a fixture the moved-spec run shows is blind, so the literal rule would defeat the test's purpose. Ruled per test: the pool test is over on two composes, the red-case test at the bar on one; the end-to-end test is FR-008's own end-to-end exception. The overrun is not a wrong outcome (constitution XIV's defect definition), and the plan states it openly with its measurements.

decisions.id: D6 the three rust/gate/crates/pool tests unchanged
decisions.summary: the real-pool tests that list a folder's ignored files by name are left as they are
decisions.why: They assert folders, rows and names, a map's kind read from tracked files, and are green in a tree with no ignored file (54 passed in the clean clone); a difference that is not a defect, which fix-all-known-bugs does not reach.

decisions.summary: which crates read generated output rests on the Cargo.toml reads, the CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR/top()/toplevel() and relative-path/current_dir greps, and a clean-clone run of the three reading crates and rust/gate
decisions.why: The search space is named per step with its method; the one thing not run (other crates) is stated as resting on the reading, and those crates' declared reads hold only caches, a fixture lockfile whose reader copies tracked files, and rust/gate's development-secrets.ini (rust/gate green in the clean clone).

decisions.id: D8 found and left none; performance work no
decisions.summary: nothing deferred; the task is not classed as performance work
decisions.why: Nothing the block reports is a defect left: the standing over-bar composing test is a timing difference, not a wrong outcome, and the gate/pool tests pass in a clean tree; the task makes a verdict tree-independent and speeds nothing, so 'no' is the plain reading.
